question:
A reverse-biased photodiode produces photocurrent proportional to absorbed photon rate. A light source of fixed power $P$ illuminates it.

At $\lambda_1=400\,\text{nm}$, quantum efficiency is $\eta_1=0.40$ and photocurrent is $I_{p1}$. At $\lambda_2=800\,\text{nm}$, quantum efficiency becomes $\eta_2=0.60$ and photocurrent is $I_{p2}$.

Assuming all other factors are unchanged, find $\dfrac{I_{p2}}{I_{p1}}$.
